what_happened: Job 20261027-054248-rjf1 (require an existing-code survey in design readings) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 1 of 3 the critic said the reading misread the request. It judged the plan's placement sound: a deterministic check_design_existing_code step in refusing_check next to check_code_survey, with a corpus case. The seams it names exist. One major finding stood. The reading claimed the reader prompt has only 3 tokens of headroom, so briefs.rs edits must not grow it. That is wrong. READING_RULES and CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE sit in the reader brief, outside BudgetSet::Reader, and the line-count test does not pin the count at 5. The plan built Decision 3 on this: it teaches the rule only through the refusal message. Nearly every design reading would then be refused on its first read and use up the one second read. It also bypasses the existing rule that each check has a reader rule line. Two minor findings: the criterion match accepts any criterion containing "existing code" and "section", even one that says the opposite; and an "Existing code:" assumption can pass by naming only the doc the job is creating. One nit: the intended-refusal test depends on the exact declaration `pub fn check_design_existing_code`. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The reading stage can state facts about the code as assumptions, here the reader prompt's headroom, and nothing resolves them against the code before the reading is accepted. The budget test covers only some briefs (CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults, catalog), but the reading treated the whole reader prompt as one budget. The planner trusted the assumption and did not recheck it. It chose to teach the rule only through a refusal, which bypasses the existing rule that every check has a reader rule line. Planning has fixed rounds and keeps no partial plan. A wrong premise therefore costs the whole planning spend, and a purely code-answerable question is never settled by a cheap check. The earlier registry class reading-edits-prompt-without-checking-token-budget is the inverse case: there the budget was ignored, here it was misread.
prevention: Add a deterministic check at reading acceptance. When a reading's assumptions state a token budget, headroom or size limit for a named prompt or brief, the check must resolve it. It computes the figure from the budget code (which constants BudgetSet covers) and rejects or corrects the assumption if it disagrees. It also requires that any new refusal check ships with a reader rule line that teaches the rule before the first read, so the reader is not taught by refusal alone. Tighten the plan-level criterion match to require a section that names real existing paths, excluding the file the job creates.
proposed_request:
Make Athena's design-reading existing-code survey rule work without refusing the first read. Outcome: a design reading must name existing code for the capability, and the reader is told this rule in its brief before it writes, so a correct design reading is accepted on the first read.

Acceptance:
- The reader brief (READING_RULES) carries a rule line for the new check, as every other check has. A test shows the rule line exists.
- A design reading with a criterion requiring an existing-code section and an "Existing code:" assumption that names at least one path that already exists in the repo is accepted. A test shows it passes.
- A reading is refused if its existing-code criterion only contains the words "existing code" and "section" but says the opposite (for example, no survey needed). A test shows it is refused.
- A reading is refused if its "Existing code:" assumption names only the file the job creates. A test shows it is refused.
- The new refusal ships with a corpus case that refuses and is declared intended, and the corpus guard passes.
- Before relying on any token-budget claim, check which parts BudgetSet::Reader covers (athena-context/src/lib.rs). READING_RULES and CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE are outside that budget. The budgets test and line-count test must still pass.
- Do not use banned words or email-like text in the added prompt text.
